subject: English Literature A
content: Love through the ages. The aim of this topic area is to encourage students to explore aspects of a central literary theme as seen over time, using unseen material and set texts. Students should be prepared for Love through the ages by reading widely in the topic area, reading texts from a range of authors and times. Areas that can usefully be explored include: romantic love of many kinds; love and sex; love and loss; social conventions and taboos; love through the ages according to history and time; love through the ages according to individual lives (young love, maturing love); jealousy and guilt; truth and deception; proximity and distance; marriage; approval and disapproval.

subject: English Literature A
content: Set texts for Shakespeare and poetry: Students study one of the following Shakespeare plays: Othello, The Taming of the Shrew, Measure for Measure, The Winter's Tale. Students study one of the following anthologies: AQA anthology of love poetry through the ages pre-1900, AQA anthology of love poetry through the ages post-1900. The paper for this component is closed book.

subject: English Literature A
content: Set texts for prose: Students study two texts from the following list: Jane Austen - Persuasion, Charlotte Brontë - Jane Eyre, Emily Brontë - Wuthering Heights, Kate Chopin - The Awakening, Jonathan Coe - The Rotters' Club, George Eliot - The Mill on the Floss, Thomas Hardy - Tess of the D’Urbervilles, F. Scott Fitzgerald - The Great Gatsby, E.M. Forster - A Room with a View, L.P. Hartley - The Go-Between, Daphne Du Maurier - Rebecca, Ian McEwan - Atonement. The paper for this component is open book. Students may take a copy of their set texts into the exam, which must not be annotated.

subject: English Literature A
content: Love through the ages. The aim of this topic area is to encourage students to explore aspects of a central literary theme as seen over time, using unseen material and set texts. Students should study three texts: one poetry and one prose text, of which one must be written pre-1900, and one Shakespeare play. Examination will include two unseen poems.

subject: English Literature A
content: Texts in shared contexts. Choice of two options: Option A: WW1 and its aftermath, Option B: Modern times: literature from 1945 to the present day. Study of three texts: one prose, one poetry, and one drama, of which one must be written post-2000. Examination will include an unseen prose extract.

subject: English Literature A
content: Option A: WW1 and its aftermath. Study of texts related to the context of World War 1 and its aftermath.

subject: English Literature A
content: Option B: Modern times: literature from 1945 to the present day. Study of texts related to the context of modern literature from 1945 to the present day.

subject: English Literature A
content: Independent critical study: Texts across time. Comparative critical study of two texts, at least one of which must have been written pre-1900. One extended essay (2500 words) and a bibliography. Assessed by teachers and moderated by AQA.

subject: English Literature A
content: Aims: The specification is designed to encourage students to develop interest and enjoyment in literary studies through reading widely, critically, and independently across centuries, genre, and gender.

subject: English Literature A
content: Assessment objectives (AOs): AO1 - Articulate informed, personal and creative responses to literary texts, using associated concepts and terminology, and coherent, accurate written expression. AO2 - Analyse ways in which meanings are shaped in literary texts. AO3 - Demonstrate understanding of the significance and influence of the contexts in which literary texts are written and received. AO4 - Explore connections across literary texts. AO5 - Explore literary texts informed by different interpretations.

subject: English Literature A
content: Assessment weightings: Paper 1 (Love through the ages: Shakespeare and poetry) - 50% of AS level. Paper 2 (Love through the ages: prose) - 50% of AS level.

subject: English Literature A
content: Assessment weightings: Paper 1 (Love through the ages) - 40% of A-level. Paper 2 (Texts in shared contexts) - 40% of A-level. Non-exam assessment (Independent critical study: texts across time) - 20% of A-level.

subject: English Literature
content: Love through the ages: The aim is to encourage students to explore aspects of a central literary theme as seen over time, using unseen material and set texts. Students should read widely in the topic area, including texts from a range of authors and times. Areas to explore include: romantic love, love and sex, love and loss, social conventions and taboos, love through history and time, individual lives, jealousy and guilt, truth and deception, proximity and distance, marriage, approval and disapproval.

subject: English Literature
content: Set texts for Love through the ages: Core set texts (Shakespeare) – Students study one of the following plays: Othello, The Taming of the Shrew, Measure for Measure, The Winter's Tale. Chosen comparative set texts (poetry and prose) – Students study two texts: one poetry and one prose text, one of which must be written pre-1900. Poetry options include AQA anthologies of love poetry (pre-1900 and post-1900). Prose options include works by Jane Austen, Charlotte Brontë, Emily Brontë, Kate Chopin, Thomas Hardy, F. Scott Fitzgerald, E.M. Forster, L.P. Hartley, Daphne Du Maurier, and Ian McEwan.

subject: English Literature
content: Texts in shared contexts: The aim is to encourage students to explore aspects of literature connected through a period of time. Students choose one of two options: WW1 and its aftermath or Modern times: literature from 1945 to the present day. Students should prepare by reading widely within their chosen option, focusing on key themes relevant to the shared context.

subject: English Literature
content: Set texts for Texts in shared contexts: Students study three texts (one prose, one poetry, and one drama), at least one of which must be written post-2000. They also respond to an unseen prose extract in the exam. Option A (WW1 and its aftermath) includes core texts like Pat Barker's 'Regeneration,' Sebastian Faulks' 'Birdsong,' and poetry anthologies such as 'Up the Line to Death.' Option B (Modern times) includes texts like Margaret Atwood's 'The Handmaid’s Tale,' Caryl Churchill's 'Top Girls,' and Carol Ann Duffy's 'Feminine Gospels.'

subject: English Literature
content: Independent critical study: Texts across time – Students write a comparative critical study of two texts on a theme of their choice. Possible themes include the struggle for identity, crime and punishment, minds under stress, nostalgia, the Gothic, satire and dystopia, war and conflict, and representations of race, gender, class, and culture. The essay must be 2,500 words, include an academic bibliography, and use appropriate referencing.

subject: English Literature
content: Tasks for Independent critical study: The word count is 2,500 words. Tasks should ensure students address all assessment objectives. An academic bibliography (not included in the word count) and appropriate referencing must be used.

subject: English Literature
content: Texts for Independent critical study: One text must be written pre-1900, and two different authors must be studied. Set texts from A-level exam components cannot be used. The essay must be comparative, with equal attention to both texts. Poetry texts can be a single longer narrative poem or a collection of shorter poems. Single-authored short story collections are permissible. Texts in translation may be used if they are influential and significant in the development of literature in English.

subject: English Literature
content: The specification encourages exploration of texts through diachronic (across time) and synchronic (within a defined time period) perspectives. It promotes a historicist approach, requiring students to read widely and connect texts across time and topic. Assessment objectives (AOs) are integrated into each question, covering text construction, contexts, connections to other texts, and interpretations. The term 'significance' is used to access AOs 2, 3, 4, and 5, involving analysis of text construction, relevant contexts, intertextual connections, and potential meanings.

subject: English Literature
content: Component requirements: Love through the ages – One Shakespeare play, one poetry, and one prose text (one pre-1900). Texts in shared contexts – One prose, one poetry, and one drama text (one post-2000). Non-exam assessment (Texts across time) – Two independently chosen texts, one pre-1900, with a comparative critical study.

subject: English Literature A
content: NEA prohibited texts: Students cannot use the following texts for non-exam assessment as they appear on the exam set text lists. The list includes authors and their works such as Margaret Atwood's 'The Handmaid’s Tale', Jane Austen's 'Persuasion', Pat Barker's 'Regeneration' and 'Life Class', William Blake's 'The Garden of Love', Charlotte Brontë's 'Jane Eyre', Emily Brontë's 'Wuthering Heights', and others.

subject: English Literature A
content: Aims: Courses based on these specifications must encourage students to develop their interest in and enjoyment of literature and literary studies as they: read widely and independently both set texts and others that they have selected for themselves; engage critically and creatively with a substantial body of texts and ways of responding to them; develop and effectively apply their knowledge of literary analysis and evaluation; explore the contexts of the texts they are reading and others’ interpretations of them. Additionally, A-level specifications must encourage students to undertake independent and sustained studies to deepen their appreciation and understanding of English literature, including its changing traditions.

subject: English Literature A
content: Assessment objectives (AOs) are set by Ofqual and include: AO1: Articulate informed, personal and creative responses to literary texts, using associated concepts and terminology, and coherent, accurate written expression; AO2: Analyse ways in which meanings are shaped in literary texts; AO3: Demonstrate understanding of the significance and influence of the contexts in which literary texts are written and received; AO4: Explore connections across literary texts; AO5: Explore literary texts informed by different interpretations. Weighting for AS: AO1 (28%), AO2 (24%), AO3 (24%), AO4 (12%), AO5 (12%). Weighting for A-level: AO1 (28%), AO2 (24%), AO3 (24%), AO4 (12%), AO5 (12%).

subject: English Literature A
content: Assessment weightings: The marks awarded on the papers will be scaled to meet the weighting of the components. For AS: Paper 1 (50 scaled marks), Paper 2 (50 scaled marks). For A-level: Paper 1 (150 scaled marks), Paper 2 (150 scaled marks), Non-exam assessment (75 scaled marks).

subject: English Literature A
content: Non-exam assessment marking criteria: Weightings for each question are AO1: 7 marks; AO2: 6 marks; AO3: 6 marks; AO4: 3 marks; AO5: 3 marks. Band descriptors include: Band 5 (Perceptive/Assured, 21-25 marks), Band 4 (Coherent/Thorough, 16-20 marks), Band 3 (Straightforward/Relevant, 11-15 marks), Band 2 (Simple/Generalised, 6-10 marks).
